name: Deadjectival Noun in -ness

1.definition: Names a property or state characterized by the base adjective.
1.details: The regular formation preserves the stress of the base. Novel formations are generally interpretable given a recognizable adjective. Some derivatives lexicalize specialized readings. Competing -ity may shift stress or alter the base.

examples.note: Constructed example with the stress of awkward preserved.

relatedConstructions.notes: The output is a common noun.
The core pattern selects an adjective as its base.
Both suffixes can create property nouns, as in kindness and opacity. The adjective base constrains the choice of suffix and can have a different stem form before -ity.

grounds.note: Documents stress, stem alternations and productivity in the two patterns.

projection.target: The regular -ness output retains base stress, and the pattern supports novel property nouns. A competing -ity formation can change the stress or shape of the base.
projection.evidence: CASA gives separate -ness and -ity records. CGEL documents their formal and productivity contrast.

curious.title: Nouns ending in -ness
curious.summary: Adding -ness to an adjective makes a noun naming the property or state the adjective describes.
curious.body: Clear is an adjective, and clearness names the property of being clear. In the clearness of the recording, the noun phrase talks about how clear the recording is. The same works with awkward and awkwardness. A regular -ness noun keeps the stress of the base word. New formations can generally be understood if the adjective is familiar, though some -ness words have specialized meanings of their own. The -ity ending competes with it: both can make property nouns, as in kindness and opacity, and -ity can change the base.
curious.try: Choose an adjective for how you feel today and add -ness. Does the new word make sense?

teacher.summary: Helps explain -ness nouns such as kindness, and how they differ from -ity nouns.
teacher.explain: The pattern forms a common noun from an adjective plus -ness, naming a property or state characterized by the adjective. The regular formation preserves the stress of the base. Novel formations are generally interpretable given a recognizable adjective, although some derivatives lexicalize specialized readings. Competing -ity may shift stress or alter the base: both suffixes can create property nouns, as in kindness and opacity, and the adjective base constrains the choice of suffix.
teacher.terms: These are sometimes treated under abstract nouns, a broader label. This dictionary treats the output as a common noun.

contrasts.note: -ity forms a property noun and can alter the base.

watch_for: A learner might think -ness and -ity can be swapped on any adjective.
A learner might assume every -ness noun means only the adjective's quality, when some have specialized readings.
teacher.activity: Students list familiar adjectives and add -ness to each, using the new nouns in sentences such as "The ___ of the ___ surprised us." They mark which words, if any, also have an -ity partner.

child.hook: What do you call being kind? What about being clear?
child.explain: You can add -ness to a describing word to name the quality. Kind becomes kindness. Kind is still right there inside kindness.

examples.text: I liked [the clearness of the recording].

child.play: Pick five describing words, like soft, bright and sad. Add -ness to each and use it in a sentence. Which new word is your favourite?

checked.note: Fixed: kindness (-ness) and opacity (-ity) no longer presented as examples of what -ity does; stress preservation stated of regular -ness formations; child line no longer claims the whole pronunciation is kept; child example with added words relabelled constructed; 'abstract nouns' flagged as a broader label. Dismissed: none. Frequency pass: teacher.summary now names kindness instead of clearness and awkwardness (about 91,500th and 37,200th in SUBTLEX-UK); constructed -ity contrast opacity (about 97,100th) replaced by ability; teacher.explain still quotes the entry's kindness and opacity; entry examples unchanged.
